datasets.description: Classic wireless sensor network with 54 motes and irregular sampling intervals.
Seven electricity transformer load channels on an hourly grid.
Three residential sub-meter channels with minute-level power readings.

conclusions: TimeSeriesFlow: Effective as an orchestration layer (14x slower than pandas on the same lightweight stats task; acceptable overhead for batch structure).

AdaptiveForecast: Partially effective: screening blocks unfit entities before training; routing assigns multiple model families where patterns differ; on UCI Household Power all entities failed gates (short span slice; screening-only outcome). Forecast accuracy was not tested.

Full stack: Partially effective when combines screening with batch orchestration and delivers per-entity routing in one pass at ~60 entities/s (+0.02s mean vs AdaptiveForecast-only loop). Not faster than pandas; value is operational plus screening, not speed.

Across 40 entities, TimeSeriesFlow is an orchestration layer (~14x pandas on stats-only work), AdaptiveForecast adds screening and routing on Intel Berkeley Lab, ETT Hourly (ETTh1), and forecast accuracy remains unmeasured. UCI Household Power blocked every entity under current gates (screening worked; not a deployment-ready forecast slice). Full-stack screening averages 60 entities/s.
pitch_highlights: Across 3 datasets, 12.5% of entities would be blocked before model training.
Mean routing diversity is 7.0% with up to 2 unique architectures assigned.
Full-stack screening averages 59.6 entities per second.
UCI Household Power: 100% training waste avoided (3 of 3 entities blocked).

timeseriesflow.headline: Effective as an orchestration layer (14x slower than pandas on the same lightweight stats task; acceptable overhead for batch structure).
effective_for: Structured per-entity batch runs with retries and progress hooks
Teams that outgrow ad-hoc groupby loops but do not need profiling yet
not_effective_for: Beating pandas on simple mean and row-count aggregates
Proving forecast quality (orchestration only in this benchmark)

adaptiveforecast.headline: Partially effective: screening blocks unfit entities before training; routing assigns multiple model families where patterns differ; on UCI Household Power all entities failed gates (short span slice; screening-only outcome). Forecast accuracy was not tested.
effective_for: Screening entities that fail quality gates before training spend
Routing labels when entity patterns differ within a fleet
not_effective_for: Replacing pandas for raw speed on simple statistics
Claims of better forecasts without a Phase 2 accuracy backtest

full_stack.headline: Partially effective when combines screening with batch orchestration and delivers per-entity routing in one pass at ~60 entities/s (+0.02s mean vs AdaptiveForecast-only loop). Not faster than pandas; value is operational plus screening, not speed.
effective_for: Nightly screening plus orchestration on heterogeneous entity fleets
Workflows that need both gate outcomes and batch runner structure
not_effective_for: Small homogeneous fleets where a single model and a pandas loop suffice
Latency-sensitive paths that only need lightweight aggregates

decision_table.criterion: Faster than pandas for the same lightweight stats task
decision_table.note: TimeSeriesFlow adds a mean 13.6x slowdown on stats-only work; profiling dominates full-stack cost.

decision_table.criterion: Blocks unfit entities before model training
decision_table.note: 5 of 40 entities blocked portfolio-wide. All entities blocked on: UCI Household Power.

decision_table.criterion: Assigns different model families per entity
decision_table.note: Mean routing diversity 7.0%; up to 2 unique families assigned.

decision_table.criterion: Forecast accuracy better than a single global model
decision_table.note: Phase 2 backtest not run. No MAE or sMAPE in this report.

decision_table.criterion: Production batch ops (checkpoints, parallel workers, retries)
decision_table.note: Benchmark used workers=1 and did not exercise checkpoint resume.

decision_table.criterion: Screening throughput for nightly fleet batches

use_when: Entity count is large enough that manual loops, retries, and progress matter
Entity quality varies and some series should be blocked before training
A single global model family is risky and per-entity routing is required
You accept profiling overhead in exchange for screening and orchestration
avoid_when: You only need exploratory mean, count, or simple aggregates on a small fleet
All entities are homogeneous and pass the same model family
You must prove forecast accuracy gains (not measured in Phase 1)
Raw pandas throughput is the primary success metric
